newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair warns Labour to toe line over Europe.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair warns Labour to toe line over Europe.

text.p: Opposition Labour leader Tony Blair told his party on Saturday to toe the line over a single European currency, saying he would not accept "personal manifestos" during Britain's forthcoming national elections.
"I do not believe you can have a group of candidates effectively standing on a separate manifesto," Blair told BBC radio in an interview.

The ruling Conservative Party is badly split by divisions on a single European currency and more than 100 Conservative candidates are expected to issue personal statements in elections which must be held by May.
Blair did not spell out what action he would take to stop Labour candidates doing the same thing but made clear he would not tolerate a "party within a party" inside Labour.
"It would not be right and it would be a breach of the Labour party's rules," he warned potential dissidents.
"If that happens, whether it's the Labour party, or the Conservative party or any party, then the public simply doesn't know what it's voting for," said Blair, who was speaking from Amsterdam.

Official Labour Party policy supports the opt-out won by the Conservatives on whether to join the single currency. Labour says it will take a decision in the national interest of Britain and will also offer voters a referendum.
Blair echoed Conservative anxieties over the possible fudging by other EU member states in meeting ecomomic targets necessary to join the single currency.

"If the proper criteria for convergence are not met, or if they're going to be fudged or bodged, then of course we have made clear all the way through it shouldn't happen and Britain wouldn't join," he said.
